openPoints: How can equality-based cell pagination remain correct after durable recovery when openDb normalizes only the current SQLite index, rebuildFromJsonl later restores legacy numeric levels from the canonical JSONL unchanged, and graph://claims?cell=auth:P4 then returns no matching claims?

What prevents two distinct history cursor flights from completing out of order and moving historyCursor or historyHasMore backward, given cursor-keyed deduplication deliberately allows those requests to run concurrently but response ownership has no generation or monotonicity guard?

What interaction-level evidence proves cell provenance, separately owned retry controls, stale loading/error rejection, and multi-page continuation behavior through og.ts and ClaimsBrowser, when the new tests assert extracted pure helpers without executing the asynchronous store and component integration?
architectureTip: Treat cursor pagination as an end-to-end contract with query-aligned indexes, generation-keyed request ownership, and interaction-level contract tests.
topFinding: Legacy claim levels are normalized only in SQLite at open time; rebuilding from canonical JSONL restores numeric levels afterward, causing the equality-based cell resource to silently hide valid claims.
